alternatives: Fat routers that call the ORM directly
data.rationale: Routers in app/api depend only on services, schemas and core. Services accept a SQLAlchemy Session plus plain config values, use repositories, and alone call commit()/rollback(). Repositories only add/flush/query. Models import only sqlalchemy. Domain exceptions live in app/core/errors.py, which keeps services free of FastAPI imports. — Meets NFR-6, makes services unit-testable without HTTP, and puts the transaction boundaries needed for the retry/replay logic (NFR-5) in one place.
data.title: ADR-1: Strict layering with services owning transactions

alternatives: Hash of the URL (deterministic, enables enumeration, conflicts with the no-dedup rule)
Pre-check with SELECT before insert (racy without the constraint anyway)
data.rationale: codes.generate_code(length) uses secrets.choice over [A-Za-z0-9]. The service inserts and flushes. On IntegrityError it rolls back and retries with a new code, up to CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 5). A reserved candidate (compared case-insensitively against RESERVED_CODES) uses up an attempt and is regenerated. When attempts run out the service raises a 503. — With 62^7 ≈ 3.5e12 codes collisions are rare. The DB constraint guarantees uniqueness across instances (NFR-5, NFR-9). Codes are unguessable (NFR-2, R-1).
data.title: ADR-2: Random base62 codes backed by a DB unique constraint and retry

alternatives: Store the full response body JSON
data.rationale: If the key exists: a matching request_hash replays the stored link (201, Idempotent-Replayed: true), and a different hash returns 409. Otherwise the link is inserted and flushed, then the key row is inserted and flushed in the same transaction, then the transaction commits. An IntegrityError on the key flush (a concurrent winner) rolls back both rows, after which the service re-reads the key and replays or returns 409. Keys are global and never expire (Q-3). Replays are rebuilt from the stored link row. — The DB constraint guarantees at most one link per key even with concurrent requests or several instances (FR-4, R-7). It never returns 500.
data.title: ADR-3: Idempotency via a table with a unique key and request hash, written in the link's transaction

alternatives: Module-level global engine with dependency overrides
data.rationale: create_app(settings=None) builds Settings() when none are given, creates the engine and sessionmaker, and stores settings, engine and session_factory on app.state. get_db(request) and get_settings(request) read from app.state. Tables are created by Base.metadata.create_all(engine) in the lifespan startup, and the engine is disposed on shutdown. — Each test gets an isolated DB by passing Settings(database_url=tmp). There are no import-time side effects and no global mutable state (NFR-7, NFR-9).
data.title: ADR-4: App factory with a per-app engine on app.state

alternatives: func.date() GROUP BY in SQL (return type differs per DB)
data.rationale: All DateTime columns are portable naive DateTime values holding UTC (models.base.utcnow() = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None)). Response schemas convert to tz-aware UTC on output. clicks_per_day fetches only created_at for rows in the window and groups by .date() in Python. top_referrers uses SQL GROUP BY referrer, followed by a deterministic Python sort and a cut to 10. — Avoids database-specific date functions and NULL ordering differences (R-6, FR-12), and gives identical serialization for replays.
data.title: ADR-5: Naive-UTC timestamps and Python-side day bucketing

alternatives: Normalize/IDNA-encode on input (violates the store-unchanged assumption)
data.rationale: The redirect handler returns Response(status_code=307, headers={'Location': url, 'Cache-Control': 'no-store'}) instead of starlette's RedirectResponse, which percent-quotes the URL. URL validation additionally rejects non-ASCII characters (clients must send punycode or percent-encoded URLs). — FR-5 requires Location to equal the stored URL exactly. Response headers are latin-1 encoded, so non-ASCII would otherwise cause 500s.
data.title: ADR-6: Raw 307 Response for redirects; ASCII-only target URLs

alternatives: Relying on FastAPI defaults (the 500 is plain text)
data.rationale: AppError subclasses carry status_code and detail: BadRequestError 400, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, GoneError 410, ServiceUnavailableError 503. Handlers are registered for AppError, StarletteHTTPException (404/405, keeping headers such as Allow), RequestValidationError (422), SQLAlchemyError (503 'Service temporarily unavailable', logged), and Exception (500). RequestLoggingMiddleware also wraps call_next in try/except: an exception is logged with its traceback and answered with 500 {"detail": "Internal Server Error"}. — Meets FR-11 and NFR-3: error bodies never contain exception text, and DB outages become 503 rather than 500.
data.title: ADR-7: Centralized JSON error handling with a middleware catch-all

alternatives: Background tasks / async queue (out of scope)
Failing the redirect when recording fails
data.rationale: After resolving an active link, the service inserts a ClickEvent and commits in its own small transaction. Any exception rolls back and is logged (logger.exception, without the IP), and the 307 is still returned. HEAD requests never record clicks. — Q-5 default: the redirect must not fail because of analytics (FR-8, R-4). HEAD is not a real visit.
data.title: ADR-8: Synchronous, best-effort click recording

data.rationale: /readyz declares db: Session = Depends(get_db) and runs db.execute(text('SELECT 1')) inside try/except Exception, raising ServiceUnavailableError('Database is not ready') on failure. If an overridden get_db itself raises a SQLAlchemyError, the global SQLAlchemyError handler returns 503 too. — Tests can simulate a DB outage through app.dependency_overrides[get_db] (FR-10). No exception text is leaked.
data.title: ADR-10: Readiness via the shared get_db dependency
